lessons: Review snagged on test coverage and a silent no-op, not on design. Keep retro.py, Window folding, suppression and the Drain hook points, and fix only the two findings.

Add tests in tests/test_retro.py that drive main(["drain"]) or _drain end to end: merge then quiescence gives exactly one tickets/retro/000001.md commit on main, effect key retro/000001, lockfile held during the commit.
Prove the rebind after self-upgrade: a handoff child running _drain must get a bound retro hook. Test it through the existing upgrade-handoff path, not a hand-built Drain.

retro_factory returns False silently when stages._driver is missing. That fails open. Expose the Driver through an explicit public accessor on the composed pipeline or Stages, and raise a construction error when it is absent.

Likely cause of the untouched regression suites: scripted test pipelines have no stages._driver, so the forced post-merge retro silently never fired. Once missing-driver fails closed, run each named suite and migrate only its listed assertion.
Drop the private runner attributes _retro_pipelines and _retro_prebuilt, which are probed from _drain. Pass the shared pipeline and Driver in through an explicit seam.
The run record must list each named regression suite and its migrated assertion. If a suite truly shows no change, give the concrete reason the forced retro does not fire there.
reason: Reviewer findings are specific, fixable oversights (missing _drain-level tests, silent no-op driver lookup, unmigrated regression suites); design is otherwise sound and scope unchanged.
